## Archive staging and name dispatch
`ftDemo_SetArchiveData(int pairs_idx,HSD_Archive* archive,int arr_idx)` selects `ftData_UnkIntPairs[pairs_idx]` and does nothing further if its data pointer is non-null. With a null pointer, selectors 0–3 use the direct string table through the source's `char***` cast; selectors 4–8 map respectively to 9, 10, 11, 14, and 15 and call `ftDemo_GetMotionFileString`. Both branches resolve an archive public symbol and store its address directly. A null result permits retry; a populated entry suppresses lookup even if archive or selector changes. It neither copies payload bytes nor stores the archive object itself. This is staging, not a globally write-once cache: `ftData_80085B98` consumes and clears the base. Later ftData motion consumers copy/parse data from derived addresses, so clearing the staging pointer is not permission to reclaim the backing payload immediately. Exact scene-level reclamation timing remains unresolved. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L136-L150 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdata.c#L1696-L1834.

There are no index guards. Negative direct selectors and extended selectors at least 9 are outside the represented domains. Even when populated data bypasses the selector table, the pair index must be valid. The relevant tables are per `FTKIND_MAX`. `Player_80036E20` maps an external character to primary and optionally secondary internal indices and forwards the same archive and selector. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdata.h#L32-L55 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/pl/player.c#L2052-L2062.

`ftDemo_GetMotionFileString(int cb_idx,int cb_arg)` returns the selected callback's result unchanged. It performs no string copy, validation, free, or direct persistent assignment; callback side effects and returned-string lifetime remain callback contracts. Missing callbacks report `no demo vi anim! %d\n` and assert. `MUST_MATCH` chooses supplied diagnostic line 296; otherwise the macro uses the current source line. Both configurations call the noreturn assertion path rather than silently returning NULL. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L152-L159 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/sysdolphin/baselib/debug.h#L11-L33.

## Facing and exceptional floats
`ftDemo_SetFacingDirection(Fighter_GObj*,float)` stores the input in `Fighter.facing_dir`, then requests Y rotation `M_PI_2 * facing_dir` for part 0. There is no normalization, clamping, wrapping, or finite-value check. Conventional ±1 inputs give opposite quarter turns; zero gives zero and other finite inputs scale continuously subject to floating conversion. NaN, infinity, signed zero, overflow, target rounding, and FP exception behavior are not specially handled or fully established here. `ftPartSetRotY` uses the primary joint unless it uses quaternion rotation, then uses `x4_jobj2`; it asserts if both use quaternion rotation. The facing field has already changed if that update fails. Part zero is proved, but exact skeletal-root identity is not. The player setter invokes this function for present transformed entity slots without checking demo slot type, so usage is not exclusive to demo fighters. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L161-L166, code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftparts.c#L1007-L1019, and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/pl/player.c#L605-L621.

The complete owned implementation and header define five public functions, the private `initFighter` adapter, a 16-entry creation callback table, and a five-entry archive-selector translation table. The header also declares `ftData_UnkMotionStates0[FTKIND_MAX]`. Canonical symbols control this review; rendered aliases are hypotheses, not independent evidence. In particular, rendered death-state names do not prove gameplay meanings for numeric demo selectors. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.h#L1-L17 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L42-L58.

## Construction and ownership
`ftDemo_CreateFighter(plAllocInfo2*)` creates a fighter-class GObj with arguments `(HSD_GOBJ_CLASS_FIGHTER,8,0)`, installs `ftDrawCommon_80080E18` at GX link 5 and priority 0, allocates Fighter and attribute-backup storage from separate pools, and attaches Fighter user data of kind 4 with `Fighter_Unload_8006DABC`. It requests character data using `internal_id`. The private adapter copies `internal_id`, `slot`, and `has_transformation` into a local `plAllocInfo`, mapping the last field to that local descriptor's `b0`, then calls `Fighter_UnkInitLoad_80068914` synchronously. This is separate from `plAllocInfo2.b0`, which chooses a costume-resource path. No descriptor address is stored by this TU; downstream retention is not proved. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L49-L79.

The constructor sets `x18=14`, installs `ftData_803C52A0` and kind-selected `ftData_UnkMotionStates0`, copies `ft_data->x14` and `x18` into `x24` and `x28`, and calls `efAsync_LoadSync` on the kind-selected entry. Descriptor `b0==0` selects `ftData_80085820`; otherwise it selects `ftData_800858E4`. Both receive initialized kind and costume ID. `Fighter_UnkUpdateCostumeJoint_800686E4` follows. The detailed distinction between the two resource helpers is not inferred from aliases.

The `unk8` selector chooses bounds `(0,9)` below 5, `(10,11)` for 5–6, `(12,12)` for 7, and `(13,13)` for 8. Values at least 9 invoke `ftData_UnkDemoCallbacks0[kind](unk8,&a,&b)` without a null check. The consumer `ftData_80085B98` establishes inclusive motion-data indices: it allocates `x59C` and `x5A0`, resets bookkeeping, reads the per-kind count, and asserts when the upper bound is at least the count. With a nonzero staged base it visits the inclusive interval, checks nonempty entry sizes against `0xB000`, assigns base-plus-offset addresses, and clears the staged base. Size equal to `0xB000` is accepted; lower bounds and reversed intervals are not validated. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L68-L98 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdata.c#L1696-L1727.

Subsystem calls then occur in this exact order: `ftParts_80074E58`, `ftParts_SetupParts`, `ftAnim_80070308`, `ftCo_800C884C`, `Fighter_80068E64`, `ftParts_800749CC`, `ftAnim_8007077C`, `ftCo_8009CF84`, `ftAnim_8006FE48`, `Fighter_UnkUpdateVecFromBones_8006876C`, and `ftCo_8009F578`. A present kind-specific `ftData_OnLoad` runs, followed by `ftColl_8007B320`, camera-box assignment from `Camera_80029020`, and `lbShadow_8000ED54`. Opaque helper internals remain unspecified rather than derived from rendered names. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L99-L116.

Persistent processes are installed as `(Fighter_8006A360,1)`, `(Fighter_procUpdate,4)`, `(Fighter_procMap,5)`, `(Fighter_8006C80C,9)`, and `(Fighter_8006D9AC,16)`. After `Fighter_UnkProcessDeath_80068354`, a non-null selected creation callback runs synchronously. Table entries 0–15 are `ftCo_800BECB0`, `ftCo_800BED88`, `ftCo_800BEF04`, NULL, `ftCo_800BEFD4`, `ftCo_800BF034`, `ftCo_800BF108`, `ftCo_800C6150`, `ftCo_800C7070`, `ftCo_800C70D0`, `ftCo_800C7178`, `ftCo_800C7220`, `ftCo_800C7294`, `ftCo_800C7308`, `ftCo_800C739C`, and `ftCo_800C7434`. Finally `ftLib_800867E8` invokes `Fighter_ResetInputData_80068854` and sets `x221D_b4=true`; it does not register the fighter with a library. The GObj is returned. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L42-L47, code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L117-L128, and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftlib.c#L377-L382.

Allocation success, valid pointers, valid kind indices, initialized model state, and usable callback output bounds are preconditions: there is no local allocation-failure return or rollback. The final creation table requires selector 0–15; checking the selected pointer for NULL does not check the index. Negative selectors take the first bounds branch but later index outside the creation table, and selectors at least 16 also exceed it. Range callbacks must initialize both bounds. Synchronous object callbacks must preserve a usable GObj because construction continues. Installed render/process/destructor callbacks have later lifetimes; the stack descriptor is not installed as their context.

`Player_80036F34` and `Player_80037054` construct stack descriptors, set `Gm_PKind_Demo`, select `b0=0` or `1`, and store returned GObjs in player entity slots. If the character mapping has an extra internal ID and its transformation flag is zero, they create a second object with `has_transformation=1`. This proves demo-player usage without assigning specific scenes to selector values. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/pl/player.c#L2080-L2132.

## Allocator initialization
`ftDemo_ObjAllocInit(void)` unconditionally calls `Fighter_800679B0`, then initializes `fighter_x59C_alloc_data` for `0xB000`-byte objects aligned to `0x20`. Ordinary first initialization instead uses `0x8000`. Common initialization configures pools, loads common data, invokes subsystem initialization, resets the spawn counter to 1, and calls present per-kind initialization callbacks. `HSD_ObjAllocInit` removes previous registrations, clears the descriptor, installs limit sentinels, computes alignment mask `0x1F` and stride `0xB000`, and reinserts it. This does not establish safety with outstanding allocations. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L130-L134, code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/fighter.c#L140-L177, and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/sysdolphin/baselib/objalloc.c#L128-L155.

## Archive staging and dispatch
`ftDemo_SetArchiveData(int pairs_idx,HSD_Archive* archive,int arr_idx)` selects a shared per-kind entry and performs no lookup if its data pointer is already non-null. With a null pointer, selectors 0–3 obtain a name through the source's `char***` cast of `ftData_803C2468`; selectors 4–8 map to 9, 10, 11, 14, and 15 and call `ftDemo_GetMotionFileString`. Both branches store the result of `HSD_ArchiveGetPublicAddress` directly. A null result permits retry; a populated entry suppresses name generation even if the archive or selector changes. There is no byte copy, payload free, or storage of the archive object itself. This is staging rather than a permanently write-once cache: `ftData_80085B98` derives selected motion-entry addresses and clears the shared base. Later motion consumers copy and parse through derived addresses, so clearing the staging pointer does not establish that backing payload memory may immediately be reclaimed. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L136-L150 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdata.c#L1696-L1834.

There are no local index guards: negative direct selectors and extended selectors at least 9 lie outside represented domains. The pair index must remain valid even when a populated entry bypasses the name tables. Relevant tables are `FTKIND_MAX` sized. `Player_80036E20` forwards the same archive and selector for a primary mapping and optionally a secondary mapping. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdata.h#L32-L55 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/pl/player.c#L2052-L2062.

`ftDemo_GetMotionFileString(int cb_idx,int cb_arg)` synchronously returns the selected callback result unchanged. It does not copy or free the string, validate its result, or directly assign persistent state. Callback effects and returned-string lifetime remain callback contracts. An absent callback reports `no demo vi anim! %d\n` and asserts. `MUST_MATCH` selects supplied diagnostic line 296; the other macro branch uses the current source line. Both enter the noreturn assertion path, not a silent NULL return. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L152-L159 and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/sysdolphin/baselib/debug.h#L11-L33.

## Facing and exceptional values
`ftDemo_SetFacingDirection` first stores the input float in `Fighter.facing_dir`, then requests Y rotation `M_PI_2 * facing_dir` for part 0. There is no normalization, clamping, wrapping, or finite-value guard. Conventional ±1 inputs yield opposite quarter turns; zero yields zero and other finite inputs scale rather than collapse to a sign. NaN, infinity, signed zero, overflow, target rounding, and FP exceptions receive no special handling here; exact target outcomes remain unresolved. `ftPartSetRotY` uses the primary joint unless it uses quaternion rotation, in which case it uses `x4_jobj2`; it asserts if both use quaternion rotation. A failure occurs after the facing field write, without rollback. Part zero is established, but its exact skeletal-root identity is not. The player-facing setter invokes this helper for present transformed entity slots without checking demo slot type, so usage is not demo-exclusive. Evidence: code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftdemo.c#L161-L166, code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/ft/ftparts.c#L1007-L1019, and code://c302741689bd67c361cd7faadb221df3193992c3/src/melee/pl/player.c#L605-L621.

## Reconciliation and limits
Independent rereading confirms the prior librarian's principal corrections: final input reset is not library registration, archive storage is consumable staging, and part zero must not be asserted to be the skeletal root. All seven section-attributed facts remain unresolved. Source proves arrays, a diagnostic literal, and the coefficient expression, not `.data`/`.sdata`/`.sdata2` placement, section extents, padding, relocations, literal representation, or register-to-parameter bindings. Rendered substitutions provide no additional proof. No gameplay names are reconstructed from numeric selectors.
